name: Nmap
what: A free network scanner for host discovery, port scanning, service and version detection, with a scripting engine for extra checks.
when: To verify which ports and services are really open on hosts you are responsible for, internally or from outside, and to confirm a firewall change did what you intended.
cost_note: Free for end users under the NPSL; embedding Nmap in commercial products needs an OEM license.
example: Get written approval and the exact list of IP ranges in scope.
Start with a discovery scan of the range: `nmap -sn 10.0.10.0/24`.
Scan live hosts for services and versions: `nmap -sV -p 1-1024 -oA scan-2026-10 10.0.10.0/24`.
Compare the open ports with your firewall rules and service inventory, and open a ticket for each unexpected service.
pitfalls: Aggressive timing and scripts can disrupt fragile devices such as printers, OT and old appliances; scan gently first.
Scanning networks you do not own or have permission for can be illegal.
Tell your SOC before you scan so the alerts are not treated as an attack.
